summary: allowForcePush leaseOnOwnBranch: may a fix task lease-push the head branch of the pull request it was filed to fix

options.description: In leaseOnOwnBranch, a lease push from the task's own worktree to the head branch recorded for that task's fixesPr is allowed; main, protected branches, forks and plain force stay refused; the developer first establishes why the push step did not push and stops with that finding if the hook need not change
Leave the mode as is; the executor reports needs-operator-push with the exact command instead of a failed verdict

body: Adopter report of 2026-11-19 (amplified-career-site, plugin 0.42.0, not reproduced here): a task filed with cli-file task --fixes-pr was refused by the lease guard when it pushed to the head branch of the pull request it fixes, because the hook accepts only ai-sdlc/<task-id>* (ai-sdlc-plugin/hooks/lib/lease-push-guard.js:235-263). DEC-0264 keeps leaseOnOwnBranch as the adopter default and does not cover a fix task's pull request branch. The pipeline push step already lease-pushes that branch outside the hook; why the executor typed the push is not verified. Draft task AISDLC-1363.
